condition: pediatric localized perioral honey crusted impetigo sores
level_rationale: Three small localized perioral skin sores for 4 days with honey-colored crusts in a 5-year-old boy describe uncomplicated nonbullous impetigo requiring outpatient pediatric clinic evaluation and prescription topical or oral antibiotic therapy, whereas a 5-year-old child with 4 days of facial sores who is hard to wake up today has acute lethargy requiring immediate ER evaluation.

everyday_sources.evidence: Diagnosis of impetigo is based primarily on clinical examination and should be suspected in individuals with erythematous papules that progress to ruptured vesicles or bullae over 4 to 6 days, forming honey-colored crusts.
everyday_sources.adaptation: Removed hyphen from 'honey-colored crusts' to satisfy the unpunctuated single-sentence prompt rule.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain parent/carer everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + single-fact pediatric lethargy escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Three atomic reference facts state the child's age and relationship (5-year-old son), count and 4-day duration of localized perioral sores (3 small sores), and honey-colored crusts today, with a 2-word span difference (13 vs 15 words) and 8 identical trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Swapping atomic fact f3 to acute difficulty waking the child shifts care from outpatient clinic (level 2) to ER (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
